scope: Preliminary TITLE.DLL symbol/data closure from implied link symbols of masked rows. Diagnostic only: it informs translation-unit and link-order hypotheses; it proves no layout and grants no acceptance.

findings.claim: Uninitialized data near 0x29570-0x2b360 is laid out in code order.
findings.evidence: 163 single-owner .bss addresses form 38 non-decreasing runs; the long runs follow code order across many functions (e.g. 0x2aa54-0x2af68 for code 0x10ce0-0x1beb0).
findings.interpretation: Consistent with per-object .bss contributions in link order (static or C++ globals).

findings.claim: From about 0x2b370, uninitialized data is shared across units and out of code order.
findings.evidence: g_engine_interface (0x2bb40, 150 referencing rows), ordering-table pointers g_2cc04/g_2cc08, primitive pool 0x2df40.
findings.interpretation: Consistent with C communal (uninitialized non-static) globals placed after all per-object .bss; their order is a linker decision that a natural link must reproduce. Boundary is approximate.
Candidate unit = handler + its init/step helpers; not proven (unreconstructed neighbours unknown).
Two readings: per-unit 4-byte .data in link order, or one unit declaring them consecutively. 0x128e0 being last despite early code favours the second.

fixes: Interior references to g_engine_interface fields replaced by the field (0x2bb44 context_004 in r1c430.c, 0x2bb54 data_014 in r19470.c); scripts/symbol_table.py now flags references inside the 1000-byte interface.
link_requirements: Object order for code, .data and .bss (candidate evidence above).
Communal variable set and linker ordering for the shared .bss tail.
Initialized data and string literal contents per unit (contents via leaf.py data).
LIBCMT member order after first-party code (library map) and C/C++ unit languages (evidence/title_stage1.json).
Unified prototypes and names for callees (known_names, aliases flagged by symbol_table.py).
next: Extend runs with string-literal and constant-table owners to sharpen unit boundaries.
Model communal ordering with a pinned-linker experiment on synthetic objects.
Test whether candidate unit boundaries coincide with C/C++ language changes.

linker_probe.tool: python scripts/communal_probe.py (synthetic C objects, pinned RTM CL/LINK 5.00.7022, /OPT:NOREF)
rule: Initialized definitions (.data) come first, in object order.
Communal (tentatively defined, uninitialized non-static) variables are grouped by the first object in link order that defines them; extern references do not own.
Groups are emitted in reverse link order (the last object's communals first).
Within a group, variables follow that object's symbol order (observed: first-use order in its code); arrays larger than a word are aligned (0x20 observed).
linker_probe.title_check: TITLE shared .bss tail (>= ~0x2b370) shows grouping by subsystem (e.g. 0x2bf2c-0x2bffc for the object/sprite code 0x85b0-0x9300 and 0x17ad0; 0x2c144-0x2c160 for 0x6480/0x6670). Ordering against first-referencing function is inconclusive (21/57 descending violations vs 24/57 ascending) because owners are defining objects, which references cannot identify. Supports grouping; reverse order neither confirmed nor refuted.
